Property-Based Benchmarking: Generated Peptides vs. Selected Database Reference Peptides

Two independent descriptions are reported: (1) compliance with the selected task-specific literature-defined ranges (no general pI cutoff), and (2) statistical similarity to the selected database reference set. For Cyclic, the primary statistical comparisons and descriptive composite distances use only Length, GRAVY, and AliphaticIndex because molecule-specific topology and modifications are absent from reference FASTA. MW, pI, and NetCharge in the descriptive tables and plots are sequence-derived exploratory approximations, not chemical properties of reconstructed macrocycles. Results are shown separately by Model and Generation Strategy.

Cyclic Descriptive Ordering under Each Descriptor Set (6 vs 5 without pI vs 3; identical records)

Important: Both six- and five-descriptor scenarios are chemically naive SEQUENCE-ONLY sensitivity analyses; removing only pI directly tests the reviewer-described perturbation. Their pI, charge and nominal MW do not describe true cyclic molecular topology. Only the three-composition-descriptor scenario is used for primary cyclic distances. Inspect changes in both distances and ranks under matched records; these tests do not establish any topology-corrected molecular ranking.

Structure applicability: CYC_BUILDER FHT examples are head-to-tail amide cycles; HIGHPLAY sequences are designed around disulfide cyclization. Disulfide closure does not automatically suppress free termini. Actual terminal caps, side-chain crosslinks, and reference-molecule stereochemistry/modifications cannot be recovered reliably from the simplified cyclic FASTA. Consequently no topology-aware molecular pI/charge/MW values are claimed, and these metrics remain excluded from primary cyclic comparisons.

Statistical Uncertainty and Robustness Audit

Bootstrap 95% percentile intervals use peptide-level resampling of published candidates and independent resampling of selected reference sequences (2,000 iterations, seed 42). These intervals and exploratory ordering frequencies are conditional on available records; they cannot correct publication/selection bias. Rank frequencies do not quantify overall model performance. n>=3 is a computational threshold, not a power guarantee. Spearman correlations and scaling/weight scenarios are exploratory. Models with fewer than 3 candidates remain descriptive only.

FASTA Input Integrity, Exact Overlap and Within-Model Similarity Audit

All FASTA inputs were checked for normalized exact-sequence duplicates (including pre-filter input counts), exact overlaps between distinct source/model groups, and within-model high similarity using normalized Levenshtein edit similarity (threshold 0.80). No observations were removed by this diagnostic audit. Exact uniqueness is not evidence of peptide independence; common generative ancestry and selection processes may remain.

Thresholds 0.80 and 0.70 are exploratory edit-similarity heuristics, not validated biological or statistical dependence thresholds. One representative per within-model connected component was retained for sensitivity calculations only; the original dataset and primary analyses were unchanged. Only comparisons retaining at least 3 sequences were retested. Shared generation runs, ancestral templates, and study-level selection can induce dependence even among dissimilar sequences. Therefore p-values and peptide-bootstrap intervals remain exploratory/conditional.

Model-Level Analysis

KDE and ECDF panels labelled EXPLORATORY (Cyclic MW, pI, NetCharge) are sequence-only diagnostics and are excluded from significance testing and descriptive composite-distance comparisons.

Plot 1 - Distribution Overlay (KDE)

Plot 2 - Empirical CDF (ECDF)

Plot 3 - Effect magnitude and BH-FDR-adjusted q-values (not an equivalence test)

Figure legend: heatmap color shows normalized Wasserstein distance (distributional effect magnitude); each cell displays the BH-adjusted Mann-Whitney q-value. Model and reference sample sizes (n) are displayed on the axes and in the associated statistical comparison table. A non-significant q-value is NOT evidence that distributions are similar or equivalent; it indicates insufficient statistical evidence of a difference. The tests are exploratory and do not establish biological or model superiority.

Generated-vs-Selected-Reference Sequence Similarity: Local Alignment

Exploratory Smith-Waterman local alignment with BLOSUM62 (gap open -10, extension -0.5), minimum 70% query coverage and at least five aligned amino-acid pairs. Identity is the matching fraction of aligned residue pairs; not BLAST or CD-HIT. The comparisons use only selected category-specific reference subsets, not full databases or model training sets. A high local identity is not a validated measure of peptide novelty. Unqualified alignments are counted separately and never treated as novel. Only head-to-tail CYC_BUILDER candidate rotations are considered; no ring/topology equivalence is assumed for disulfide-closed HIGHPLAY. Chemical modifications are unavailable. Reference leave-one-out and composition-shuffled sequences provide exploratory baseline comparisons.

Method Notes

  • Literature-defined ranges: selected task-specific reported thresholds only; no universal pI compliance range is imposed.
  • Cyclic chemistry: CycPeptMPDB FASTA represents mapped amino acid identity only, not connectivity, stereochemistry, termini, or modifications. Thus primary cyclic statistical tests and descriptive composite-distance comparisons are based on Length, GRAVY and AliphaticIndex only. Sequence-derived MW, pI and NetCharge remain exploratory and are not interpreted as actual molecular values. Head-to-tail closure removes free terminal ionization; disulfide closure does not itself remove termini, and actual terminal caps and linked residues matter. No topology-specific values were fabricated.
  • Multiple comparisons: BH-FDR applied separately for Mann-Whitney and KS within each peptide category, across eligible model-by-descriptor comparisons; separate test families are used for strategy-level analyses. Non-significance does NOT prove similarity or equivalence.
  • Ranking and uncertainty: Smaller observed composite distance denotes only greater descriptive similarity of these selected sequence sets to the specified reference on included descriptors; overlapping bootstrap intervals and descriptor-sensitive differences do not establish statistically or biologically superior generative models.
  • Environment: Biopython 1.86 is required and checked at run time. Reference FASTA files are externally constructed inputs; integrity checks do not independently reproduce database acquisition, filtering, or sampling. Please retain the source files, metadata and versioned construction scripts separately.
  • Selection caveat: Dataset includes available, sequence-identifiable, literature-reported candidates, not standardized random samples from full generator outputs. Published candidate selection and validation vary across studies.
  • Redundancy: Length/MW may correlate, so six marginal descriptor distances do not constitute six independent lines of evidence. Normalization by a small reference SD can magnify an attribute.
  • Independent runs: The dataset contains reported candidate sequences rather than reproducible standardized outputs from the underlying model weights, training configurations, and common sampling protocols. No independent model-generation runs were performed; the supplied code only recomputes analysis on available candidate sets.
  • Scaling applicability: For Cyclic, the primary descriptors are Length, GRAVY and AliphaticIndex, so MW-exclusion and Length/MW-downweighting scenarios do not apply; reference-IQR scaling is evaluated instead.
  • Per-property effect sizes: Normalized Wasserstein distance and bootstrap 95% percentile intervals are reported per eligible descriptor; estimates are withheld for n<5 and remain exploratory for low N.
  • Small samples: Rug marks replace smooth KDE for model groups with fewer than 10 observations; ECDF conveys observed discrete sample sizes. n>=3 does not assure sufficient power.
  • Mann-Whitney U test: non-parametric test for whether values are drawn from the same distribution as the selected category-specific database reference subset.
  • Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: tests for differences in overall distribution shape/location.
  • Wasserstein distance (normalized by selected reference-set SD): continuous measure of distance; 0 = identical.
  • Compliance %: percentage of values falling inside the 5th-95th percentile range of the selected category-specific reference peptides.
  • Model vs. Strategy: Category is biological; Strategy is a generation-method dimension, tracked independently since one strategy can produce peptides across multiple categories.
